purpose: Align every durable estate to the post-Cold War phase model, conversion stages, recurring archetypes, decisive records, report contracts, and falsification obligations without changing estate custody, graph state, or publication state.
alignment_rules: Every estate must map to at least one historical phase, conversion stage, archetype, report contract, decisive record family, and falsification question.
Alignment is a research-routing layer, not evidence that a phase, archetype, conversion, or intentionality level is established in that estate.
An estate may support several conversion stages, but one complete conversion chain requires independently receipted links among stages.
Intentionality is reviewed actor by actor and instrument by instrument; estate membership cannot assign an intentionality level.
Existing denominators, controls, nulls, counterweights, and unsuccessful paths remain mandatory.

priority_questions: Which bounded events, drafts, appointments, contracts, or filed interests convert roster adjacency into material co-participation?
Which concepts, actors, and supplier categories crossed from private convening into public policy or procurement?
estates.falsification_question: Do complete bounded events and comparator convenings show ordinary networking without material policy, gate, or transaction conversion?

priority_questions: How did defense reviews and industrial strategies alter supplier universes, requirements, and public-private implementation mechanisms?
Which contracts, standards, data rights, and substitution provisions determine practical control?
estates.falsification_question: Were requirements independently formed, broadly competed, and implemented through genuinely substitutable government-controlled architectures?

priority_questions: Who formed the supplier and product option set before formal acquisition gates?
Which requirement, evaluation, acceptance, data-rights, ordering, accreditation, and interface-control records made a private architecture durable?
Did public validation and enterprise adoption create practical dependence or preserve meaningful substitution?
decisive_record_families: obligations, outlays, performance, protests, and unsuccessful bids
estates.falsification_question: Do complete decision files show independent requirements, meaningful competition, government control of data and interfaces, and practical vendor replacement?

priority_questions: How did planning narratives, authorities, public infrastructure, and finance convert land positions into durable private development rights and value?
Who retained title, debt priority, default rights, tax advantages, and appreciation after public commitments?
estates.falsification_question: Do same-regime controls show ordinary development outcomes, symmetrical treatment, public recovery rights, and no unusual transfer of residual value?

priority_questions: Which firms recur across allied cohorts, investors, test centers, national accelerators, and awards after exact legal-entity resolution?
Does cohort recurrence predict public validation beyond ordinary comparator rates?
estates.falsification_question: Does a complete allied cohort and award denominator show no advantage beyond ordinary technical and market selection?

priority_questions: Which policy-authorship, personnel-transfer, supplier, and implementation records connect private agenda formation to state AI capacity?
Which private platforms became shared services or operating layers, and what public substitution capacity remained?
estates.falsification_question: Do records show independent public authorship, ordinary supplier selection, public operating capacity, and no durable private control layer?

priority_questions: Did role transitions place the same people in agenda, selection, evaluation, implementation, and later-benefit positions?
Were disclosures, recusals, waivers, and communication boundaries complete and effective?
estates.falsification_question: Do complete role and matter records show clean separation, effective recusals, and ordinary career movement without decision participation?

priority_questions: How do legislation, appropriations, committee activity, campaigns, lobbying, and disclosed financial interests intersect at exact entity and decision windows?
Are nonmatches and ordinary political-finance patterns preserved?
estates.falsification_question: Do complete disclosures and decision windows show ordinary diversified holdings, no matter-specific participation, and no unusual legislative benefit?

priority_questions: Which boards, authority powers, procurement actions, property transactions, and disclosures convert public authority into private control or value?
Were counterparties, unsuccessful paths, and officeholder interests fully resolved?
estates.falsification_question: Do complete transaction and comparator records show ordinary authority operations, arms-length terms, and effective public oversight?

priority_questions: How do authorization, ceiling, obligation, outlay, milestone, performance, recovery, and private residual rights differ across programs?
Which public investments created markets, protected incumbents, or retained meaningful public control?
estates.falsification_question: Do recipient and comparator ledgers show proportionate private risk, effective milestones, public recovery, and no durable asymmetry in rights or upside?

priority_questions: Did regulator, adviser, industry, and later-employment roles overlap with matter-specific approvals, enforcement, or market formation?
Which regulated classifications or workflows became compulsory, and what appeal existed?
estates.falsification_question: Do complete matter records show independent regulation, effective recusals, consistent treatment, and meaningful appeal?

priority_questions: Which legal vehicles, financing rounds, boards, preferences, strategic rights, acquisitions, and portfolio controls shaped the supplier option set?
What rights were actually held and exercised, rather than inferred from a portfolio listing?
estates.falsification_question: Do filed rights and complete portfolio denominators show ordinary venture practice without unusual gate-shaping, governance, or public-benefit concentration?

priority_questions: Which official registries confirm ownership, officer, intermediary, address, and transaction roles?
Do entity chains obscure control or simply reflect ordinary legal and investment structures?
estates.falsification_question: Do official records resolve apparent opacity into ordinary, lawful structures without hidden control or public-benefit transfer?

priority_questions: Which public-interest artifacts can be authenticated and joined under exact, predicate-specific identities?
Which crossings materially change a conversion-chain interpretation rather than merely adding notoriety?
estates.falsification_question: Do authenticated and predicate-separated records fail to support the proposed crossing once identity, dates, and ordinary explanations are resolved?

priority_questions: Which protests, cases, settlements, dismissals, appeals, and dispositive instruments confirmed or rejected proposed conversion-chain links?
What unsuccessful claims and no-case controls constrain the thesis?
estates.falsification_question: Do dispositive records reject, narrow, or independently explain the alleged gate, control, coercion, or extraction mechanism?

priority_questions: Which exact client, matter, date, legal entity, and service type connects an intermediary to a conversion stage?
Did legal, lobbying, consulting, audit, placement, or compliance roles shape public gates or merely perform ordinary services?
estates.falsification_question: Do complete engagement and ordinary-client denominators show no matter-specific role in option formation, public conversion, or control architecture?

priority_questions: Which grants, boards, related organizations, fiscal sponsors, and policy programs shaped agendas and eligible actors?
Did nonprofit legitimacy and funding convert into public adoption or private benefit?
estates.falsification_question: Do complete grant and board chronologies show ordinary philanthropy without coordinated option formation, public conversion, or beneficiary concentration?

priority_questions: How did public research awards become patents, assignments, licenses, spinouts, private capital, and government contracts?
Who retained intellectual property, governance, and residual value?
estates.falsification_question: Do complete research and licensing records show fair public returns, ordinary commercialization, and no unusual concentration of control or benefit?

priority_questions: Who controls models, data, cloud, compute, accreditation, deployment, assurance, and retirement across public systems?
Did a tool become a shared service, integration layer, mission operating system, ecosystem host, or mandatory substrate?
decisive_record_families: portability, substitution, termination, and retirement records
estates.falsification_question: Do system records show modular use, public control, open interfaces, practical migration, and no mandatory or irreversible private operating layer?

priority_questions: How do facilities, load, rates, utility ownership, interconnection, public approvals, and operating obligations enable strategic private capacity?
Who bears infrastructure and stranded-asset risk?
decisive_record_families: public contribution, recovery, and failure records
estates.falsification_question: Do complete rate, interconnection, and ownership records show ordinary infrastructure provision, proportionate private risk, and effective public recovery?

priority_questions: Which dated legal authorities, designation versions, licenses, exclusions, and transaction identities constrained markets or ownership?
Who benefited from or was compelled by the resulting market boundaries?
estates.falsification_question: Do versioned lists, licenses, and adjudications show consistent public-law application without selective market creation or private benefit?

priority_questions: Which assignments, licenses, standards roles, government-rights clauses, interface baselines, and substitution terms allocate durable control?
Can public institutions operate, modify, compete, and migrate without the rights holder?
estates.falsification_question: Do operative rights and interface records show broad government rights, open standards, practical substitution, and no durable private lock-in?

priority_questions: Which exact employers, people, positions, appointments, worksites, visas, labor certifications, and post-employment roles form the talent-routing system?
Did public missions create private labor advantages or coercive workforce dependencies?
estates.falsification_question: Do exact cohort and comparator records show ordinary labor mobility, lawful recruitment, and no unusual conversion of public roles into private advantage?

priority_questions: Which deeds, mortgages, leases, liens, UCC records, easements, releases, and beneficial interests determine durable control and residual value?
How did public approvals or infrastructure alter title, debt priority, and exit?
estates.falsification_question: Do instrument-level title and debt chains show ordinary financing, transparent ownership, effective public protections, and no unusual private residual transfer?

programs.objective: Add first-class problem-frame, option-set, conversion-event, control-right, dependency, residual-value, and reversibility objects without changing the bounded-hop kernel.
Tag cases, claims, events, instruments, and reports to overlapping historical phases with explicit dates and no causal inference from phase membership.
Review actor-specific propositions through the six-level intentionality ladder with separate evidence, falsifiers, and counterevidence at each level.
Build comparative views of data, ontology, interface, accreditation, IP, governance, title, debt, substitution, termination, and public operating rights.
Extend structured reports with doctrine, option-set, conversion, control, compulsion, residual, and falsification panels while retaining canonical claim and review law.
